uniequip_002_lumen:
On Jordi's lower leg is an already almost indiscernible scar, left when he was nine years old.
Young Jordi always loved to sit on the benches that lined the town plaza, hugging his knees, spacing out as he stared at the lighthouse statue in the plaza's center. Whenever he did, he did so for the whole day. Jordi had carefully chosen his position, and watching from this angle at sunset, the sinking sun in the west would line up with the tip of the lighthouse for the briefest moment, like this tiny little lighthouse too had come alight.
Regrettably, it was a fleeting scene, and in the span of a few short breaths, the lighthouse statue would once again go out. Everything about it would be rapidly shrouded in shadow, engulfed by darkness. What he had just witnessed was much like an illusion, gone without a trace.
Fortunately, the sun would rise as it did before the next day, and the lighthouse would come alight again. Just for a moment, of course.
On the day of his ninth birthday, Jordi decided to do something big. He wanted to grab hold of something more lasting. He'd try and see for himself what the town's elder workers were so proud of yet kept so secret, see for himself the colossal structure the parents he'd never met had disappeared in, see for himself that true 'Eye of Iberia.' Jordi began to climb the statue in the plaza, believing as long as he stood on its top, he'd be able to see the true rays of the lighthouse piercing through the fog. He clambered inch by inch, hearing the passersby in the plaza shrieking frantically, but the top was right there before him, he just had to make one final leap...
Jordi suddenly felt himself falling—the protrusion he'd used as footing likely crumbled—but why he was falling was no longer important. Jordi had struggled so he could cast his sight far away. Even if it was only for a split-second, he wanted to see it.
Nothing. There was nothing. The fog was like a gauze, covering all upon the surface of the sea.
When Jordi came to, he was already back at home, his leg bandaged, the scent of meat porridge pervading the room. Hearing the sound of Jordi turning over, Thiago poked his body out of the kitchen. Jordi thought he'd be in for a ferocious scolding, but Thiago simply stared at him for a moment, let out a sigh, and pointed in the direction of the desk. There was laid a spyglass, glittering in alluring bronze.
That was a bygone affair, years and years ago, and now the scar has even faded. Only the small town's plaza seems to have been overlooked by time, resting unchanged. Jordi sits in his younger self's most favorite spot. Now he's seen the true Eye of Iberia, yet he can no longer sit on this bench with his uncle, listening to those heart-racing stories, taking turns at the spyglass through which they'd gaze far away.
But even with the help of a spyglass, they still couldn't see anything. It was the one thing the two of them silently, tacitly, never mentioned to each other.
uniequip_003_lumen:
To the Inquisition has come an Ægir.
I can assure you, not for the past thirty years... no, forty, at the very least! Has an Ægir set foot in the Inquisition's court in any capacity other than that of the tried. The very words themselves are preposterous.
It was a young man, not particularly remarkable at first glance. Of fair height, but didn't stand too straight or firm. His features were proper, but lacked any good presence. In all regards, not someone especially worth minding. If it weren't for the fact he was an Ægir, I think even someone new like myself wouldn't have batted an eye at him, with how unassuming and overt his arrival was.
But now, all the Inquisition is abound with the rumor of this Ægir.
Some say he's some wicked convict's bosom friend, merely held temporarily in custody, but this young man—before I forget, his name is Jordi Fontanarossa—clearly has no restrictions placed on his movements. Others believe he's a signal from Lord Carmen that the Inquisition is once again to admit and even promote some of the Islanders in due time. However, Jordi Fontanarossa himself is feeble and weak, and his education lacking. At best, he would be capable of some meager secretarial work, and it doesn't seem as if his position is particularly lofty.
Given our workplaces are so near each other, I've had the opportunity to observe him.
This Ægir punches in at twenty minutes before his shift each morning, sometimes a little later, but he's never tardy. He's prone to occasional clumsiness; he once caused a misprint of documents after poorly operating the press, wasting quires of business paper. If I hadn't chanced to pass by and stop the machine, who knows how his accident could have evolved.
I wasn't going out of my way to help him, of course, simply taking responsibility for our work. And no matter how I explained to him as such, the Ægir just persisted with his smile. He'd clearly misunderstood something! Such a loathsome smile!
One time, in relation to a vital operation, some colleagues and I were working overtime into the night. The Ægir brought a bucket of drinks over, telling us it was some herbal tea he'd mixed himself. I wasn't interested in having any, but that sort of thing is effective at keeping one awake, so for the sake of work, it would have to do.
It was about early morning by the time we were done with overtime, and everyone was audibly starving, running on bellies filled with nothing but tea. There in the dark, I suddenly heard footsteps approach, then saw someone had lit a lantern. It was that Ægir, who himself hadn't left for some reason, and had a pot in his hands too, with several bags clearly filled with food hanging from his wrists.
'Ah, are you all done with work? You must be exhausted.'
The man seemed all too apologetic as he regarded us. 'I'm sorry I couldn't be of help with any of it. All I could do was make some food that'd be light on the stomach...'
With no patience for hearing out his habitual self-debasement and humbling excuses, I took his pot without any fanfare.
It was a vanilla porridge, and all signs pointed to it being yet another recipe beneficial to health.
Lord Carmen having taken in this Ægir as a disciple? Absolutely never would I lend credence to such a ridiculous rumor. That said, based on what I've seen, should the Inquisition decide it would readmit Islanders, I suppose it would hardly be a bad thing.
uniequip_002_agoat2:
[Recording: Bubbling lava]
Title: Volcano's Breathing
Description:
When the Mount Siesta stopped erupting, Professor Keller and I climbed up the volcano once again to finish our last data collection.
After we recorded this sound of bubbling lava, Professor Keller suddenly suggested that we sit for a while at the mountaintop.
She gazed at the already ash-grey Siesta and I saw her eyes swell up with tears. She mentioned something about the future of the Volcano Museum of Siesta and her plans for retirement, which would very likely be delayed. I knew that she wanted me to visit Siesta as much as possible in the future—not just for research.

[Recording: Singing with music]
Title: Singing at a Cake Shop
Description:
It's been a while since I last came back, and I had this feeling that this little town was stuck in time and nothing was ever going to change.
However, I accidentally noticed that the cake shop Mom used to like so much had finished its renovation and reopened. A lot of musicians even came to the courtyard, holding impromptu performances.
I heard a very familiar melody that day and went up close, and the singer invited me to join them! *Sighs* It was a pity I couldn't remember the lyrics and wasn't quite sure which part everyone was singing, so I just struggled to hum along... Hope I wasn't off-key too much.

[Recording: An academic talk]
Title: On-campus Seminar
Description:
I brought the data from Mount Siesta back to Wilhelm University and met with Dr. Kahn and other scholars there. Dr. Kahn seemed a little unsettled. I told him it was not a big deal, but by the looks of it, that wasn't much help.
Thankfully, after some small talk, we started discussing research on volcanoes, and Dr. Kahn finally found peace and became more relaxed.
The seminar was exciting. No one seemed to care that we were not in a classroom, laboratory, or meeting room, but just standing on a path on campus.
It felt really nice.

[Recording: Ripped audio from a childhood video]
Title: I Still Remember That Wish
Description:
I left the university and came back home.
I changed the curtains, threw away some old stuff I didn't need anymore, and found a childhood video in the process. It was a shame that most of the content was damaged. Fortunately, the soundtracks were intact, so I got to rip them and re-record them onto this tape.
I heard Mom and Dad singing me the birthday song and encouraging me to make a wish. Of course, I didn't say it out loud, but I still remember it—
Now I'm on my way to making it come true.

[Recording: Friends' laughing]
Title: A Welcome Party For Me!
Description:
I returned aboard for my regular check-up after settling everything at home. It'd been a long time since I last left Rhodes Island, and guess what? People held a welcome party for me!
Provence and Angelina caused a little chaos when they set off the firework tubes and accidentally knocked down a huge pile of dolls. Then next thing I remember was little lambs coming from nowhere and rampaging all about... It was a disaster. But everyone was laughing so hard.
I really hope these kinds of moments can last longer.

[Recording: N/A]
Title: Untitled
Description:
For the next field investigation.
I'd love to keep more recordings if I have the chance—the sound of lava, wind, rain, and the people around me.
uniequip_003_agoat2:
[Name] Marshmallow 3

Rapid color change in stem cross-section observed when soil Originium levels above threshold, allowing for quicker detection of impending volcanic eruption compared to previous petal observation method.
[Cultivation and Management] To ensure sample quality and quantity, and to maintain consistency with field environment, the research team employed genetic resource preservation, with regular cultivation managed by specialists with the support of Wilhelm University's College of Geology and the Rhodes Island office in New Siesta. Regular reviews are still required to ensure smooth cultivation and breeding. See the appendix for details.
[Addendum] Staff reported that some kind of creature had been chewing the plants, but nothing appeared on the camera feeds. After a review, Adele provided the following recommendations:
1. Put fresh grass, fruit, and ice cream on a dining table. There should be different fruits and ice cream each day, with no repetition in any given week;
2. Keep the break room TV on at all times. Tune it to Siestan Traffic at 8 A.M., Volcano's Kitchen (Junior Edition) at noon, and Love in Siesta at 8 P.M. daily (program updated on a regular basis);
3. Check your personal belongings daily; if anything is missing, place extra marshmallows on the dining table the following day and check your own pocket the day after. Report and hand in any unknown items you find.
For staff members who were still skeptical, Adele left these words—
'There's no malice in it; they're just curious. Sometimes I can't help but think... The lava running down the mountainside when a volcano erupts is like the land's exposed blood vessel. You can almost hear a massive heart beating underground, trying to tell us something, only we don't understand yet. Perhaps they, like us, are hoping that these flowers will grow and evolve, and translate the language of Terra for us.'
uniequip_002_reed2:
Feeling in the dark, Reed untangles her hair with utmost care, then stands herself straight once more.
A dream comes to mind, one she always used to have. Her sister stands behind her in her shadow, watching as she puts on a deathly heavy crown. She feels it's wrong for her to be wearing it, but she can't take it off no matter how she tries; all she can do is melt it by fire. Metal trickles down her face, scalding, searing, but the idea of the purple flame bringing her comfort, ice-cold, scares her more. So she makes not a sound.
And she recalls two people she met while pursuing the high-speed battleships' tracks a few days ago, ordinary folk. They knew the name of Dublinn—their land showed scars from being razed by fire. They asked Reed point-blank, are you the one who ruined our lives? The Draco, manipulator of the flame of life, fell silent for a while. She was familiar with the fear her sister could leave in people. But in the end, she nodded, for she is the Leader of Dublinn, and the Tarans have no need for two Dublinns.
Someone is calling her name. She leaves, through the tight wooden door.
—She crosses a threshing floor, filled with hay and cardboard stage props of every color.
Her costume's a little cumbersome—everyone wanted to drape their own two sashes over her, in much the manner one nestles two flowers for their beloved in a buttonhole. Surely the Red Dragon didn't take to the battlefield like this a millennium ago.
But no matter. They don't have to trouble themselves with the looks of the crown-bearer. Let the wandering minstrels suppose, for the sake of a rhyme, that the Draco hero of legend had hair just as flowing and golden.
Reed clears her throat and swishes her tail, a little wary. The Tarans in front of her don't know how each brook of muddy waters tracing through the marsh is the track of a galloping warship. They don't know that the bleak clouds to the north that never blow this way are the fumes of war. They don't know that what Reed grasps is the very flame of the Red Dragon of Tara. They simply know it's important to still have food to eat after their taxes are levied, and it's as important to make sacrifice and perform theater so their farmwork is bountiful and blessed. Sat in the back are the soldiers who've fought all the way alongside her, and they look at her just as expectantly. They've taught Reed that a failure to learn the lines means no good harvest in the coming year.
'I give you land, and I give you the weather to nurture it.'
A fire ignites at her speartip in time with her words, and the audience abruptly settles down. At this moment, all could swear they have some vague premonition as to who it is that stands before them.
Reed lowers her head. A child places a floral garland on her head of every color under the sun, each flower a symbol of a growing, flourishing crop.
It is light, almost weightless. She bows down, and to the village's script, unchanged in all its years, she adds one line.
'I give you peace.'
uniequip_002_titi:
Returning to Menat-Ha'mait from Trimounts takes at least three months. She could hitchhike with mercenary caravans in Columbia, but the journey home got harder once outside the country. Only after wasting several days at a border town does she finally find a caravan headed the right way back.
Titi makes friends with the caravan leader in just a few days, a dark-skinned Liberi called Inam. She is quite curious about Titi's solo journey, as well as her past experiences.
'A Sargonian going to Columbia to study is rare enough, but for such a niche major? And now you're even headed home? Why?'
'Well, I did get scouted by a few Columbian museums after I graduated, but... I still feel 'Sargonian'. Besides, all my best friends are back home.'
'But you haven't seen them in years, have you?'
'We grew up together. We would play pranks on each other, but also help each other sneak out to play. They've kept in touch with me during my time in Columbia too. I know Pepe's an archaeologist now, leading a dig in the south, while Anat's life has probably been arranged by her father, but I'm sure she'll break free from that and do what she really wants—she's always talked about traveling the land and seeing what's outside Sargon.'
'So everyone has a goal in mind.'
'Well, they do. As for me, my family likes to say my heart's as fickle as the sands, easily swayed by a gust of wind. I went to study in Columbia on a whim, but to be honest...'
Titi can still remember the night of her father's funeral. Her mother went to rest once all the guests were gone, leaving her alone in her father's study. The chair he used to occupy was now empty, and she realized for the first time how scary the bookshelves she used to take lightly were. Every shelf was crammed with tomes, as if they could burst free at any moment and crash down on her bewildered self.
At that moment, she heard a familiar knocking sound from the window. A secret code used with her friends.
Then, Pepe nimbly opened the window and climbed into the study with Anat in tow. With a surprised expression, Titi recalled her mother bidding farewell to them earlier, along with their parents.
'Titi... you didn't eat much earlier, did you? We got you some food.' Anat took out two pieces of sun bread, handing one each to Titi and Pepe. 'You have one too.'
The sun bread was filled with Titi's favorite orange flavor, and reminded her of her empty stomach. When she finally took her first bite, Pepe seemed to heave a sigh of relief, and took a bite from her own as well, although she immediately grimaced.
'Anat, you jerk! What did you stuff into mine?!'
Anat smiled shyly. The two began to squabble with exaggerated, almost theatrical movements. Titi could see they were clearly acting it out. Amidst their laughter and playful antics, a warmth seeped back into the study.
'I think... I can help them realize their own dreams first. Then I'll figure out what I want to do myself.'
uniequip_002_monstr:
You're hurt.
As you leaf through the documents, the paper slices open your skin at one particularly tricky angle.
It's no big deal. You didn't even feel it.
At least, not until Mon3tr comes in with a new stack of documents.
At first, she simply stops and looks around, left and right, like she senses something wrong in the office.
When she grabs your wrist, snatches away your pen, and flips your hand over, you finally see the cut on your index finger.
It's not deep, and barely a drop of blood has oozed out. Your body's natural healing processes are already doing their job. It'll probably be fully healed with just a band-aid and a day's wait.
But it's obvious the medical consultant before you thinks otherwise.
Thanks to nearly all your prior treatments being handled by Kal'tsit, Mon3tr has a very thorough understanding of your body's condition. Kal'tsit had, naturally, handled more serious injuries than this. Sometimes with a bandage, sometimes with medical gel, and on very rare occasions, with direct use of her healing gun.
But what should she do now?
There is nobody who can give her an answer.
Mon3tr is left thinking for quite a while, your hand firmly clasped in hers the entire time. Based on the look on her face, you get the feeling that if you don't help her out of this conundrum, she would end up running around with you on her back, searching for the Sarcophagus.
Which is why you point at a small first-aid kit to your side, stocked with everything you need for basic medical treatment.
Move, search, select, use. In relief, she follows your 'orders'.
After using a cotton swab to disinfect the wound, she gently yet deftly plasters on a band-aid. Once done, she cups your hand in hers, mumbling something to herself as she softly pats your palm. Then, she is gone, before you even have the chance to thank her.
...
You had assumed that little incident was behind you, but twelve hours later, as you supervise the construction of a new plate with a hard hat on your head, she suddenly pops up beside you, ripping off your band-aid.
The remaining shallow mark does not seem to satisfy her, so she stuffs another one into your hands.
Another twelve hours later, as you are brewing up some fresh coffee, you see Mon3tr waving at you as she walks by. An action with a deeper meaning beyond a simple greeting, of course. And so, you wave back, showing her your healed finger. This way, both you and she will enjoy a peaceful night's rest—
At least, that's what you thought. It's just that, the moment you start sipping your coffee, she is already sitting by your side.
'Does it still hurt?'
You shake your head, showing her your formerly-injured finger as you give it a good rub with another, doing your best to assuage her worries.
'But my memories tell me that bleeding hurts a lot. What does it feel like?'
You look at her puzzled expression, and you know you should find some other way to satisfy her thirst for knowledge.
How much did it hurt this time? You ask her to hold out her hand, then you run your fingernail firmly across her index finger. You then turn her question back at her.
Does it hurt?
The answer is, of course, no. The most she does is scratch at her finger a little due to a minor itch. Her heart is now calmed, but her tone of voice takes a turn for the strange as she 'warns' you that any bodily abnormalities must be reported to her ASAP.
Naturally, you agree, and as thanks, you offer her a simple but delicious midnight snack.
uniequip_002_amiya3:
Kal'tsit pauses at the door of the command center.
'Dr. Kal'tsit?' The girl inside takes notice.
She lifts her head in an attempt to catch Kal'tsit's gaze. However, stacks of files sprawled across the conference table obscures most of her face, revealing only the tips of a pair of fluffy ears.
'The leader of the Leithanian convoy did not object to our terms.' Kal'tsit listens as she moves towards the girl, gathering the scattered files. 'That doesn't mean they'll agree to all of them.'
'Right. While they were polite during the negotiations, the way they looked at me felt... cold and menacing.' The girl winces, as if still feeling the sting of their sugar-coated animosity.
'Try not to—'
'—be influenced by the emotions of others, especially their negative ones. I understand.' The girl's smile is reassuring. 'Don't worry. I've already put them under the surveillance of Mantra's squad. Logos assured me that if they harbored any ill intentions towards Rhodes Island, their hands would be frozen to their staffs before they could even cast.'
Logos likely tempered his rhetoric when describing the devastating effects of his Arts to protect this young girl. It has become a common practice among the Operators, who adjust to her leadership while subconsciously taking her as a child who needs protection. Yet anyone who assumes that eleven-year-old Amiya needs protection is soon taken aback by her shrewdness and meticulous nature.
Young Amiya is growing quickly. She has already outgrown her bespoke dress from three months ago, and the rate at which her mind expands is even more remarkable. There were times when Kal'tsit felt that each day, the Amiya she saw was slightly different from the day before. She wasn't sure if it was merely a hallucination or if the influence of Civilight Eterna on Amiya hadn't been completely subdued.
'Dr. Kal'tsit...' Amiya's voice softened, like a pin dropping in a silent room. 'I've been dreaming again.'
'What did you dream about?'
'I dreamed of... a person. She sat next to me, held my hand, and spoke of many things. Some were from my past, while others seemed like experiences yet to come.'
'The future?'
'Umm... Maybe. She told me that in a massive nomadic city with steel high walls, a terrible war will break out. Many, especially the Sarkaz, will perish, and black rocks will spread everywhere.'
'And as she spoke of these things, she was...'
'She was so very upset, but she was strong and didn't keep crying. She said she would never give up and that the future would become better.'
Kal'tsit extends her hand to the little girl. In the past year, the deceased have not been a topic commonly discussed. Perhaps Amiya still needed comfort to cope with her losses.
'Amiya, it is only natural to miss those we've lost. You need not suppress your feelings for Theresa.'
'Well... I do miss Theresa a whole lot, but it wasn't her in my dream.' Amiya's eyes widen. 'Dr. Kal'tsit, I think... the person in my dream was me.'
Kal'tsit is slightly taken aback by this revelation, but before she can respond, Amiya has already rushed forward and embraced her.
'All this talking has made me hungry.' The young girl shakes Kal'tsit's hands, her eyes shining with a precious look. She begins to drag Kal'tsit along, her voice bubbling with excitement. 'Dr. Kal'tsit, won't you keep me company?'
'What should we get? Baked beans sound nice. Mr. Scout said that adding carrots would make them sweeter...'
'Brr... Ursus sure is cold. Do you think those who sit around all day feel cold too?'
'Say, Dr. Kal'tsit, do you ever... Dr. Kal'tsit...'
Kal'tsit holds onto Amiya's hand, allowing herself to be led. As Amiya's cheerful chatter fills the air, Kal'tsit finds herself lost in thought—
Closure has done an impressive job with the landship. The lights in this corridor are so much brighter now.
